## Example 3.29 {#fv7-example-3-29 .fv-lesson .sphere-lesson }

```{=html}
<p class="sphere-small">2024 Kambala Mathematics Extension 2 Trial, Q13(c) — 3 marks</p><p>Find the points of intersection of the line</p><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{r}(\lambda)=\begin{bmatrix}5\\1\\-3\end{bmatrix}+\lambda\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\\-2\end{bmatrix}"></span></div><p>with the sphere</p><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="(x-3)^2+(y-2)^2+(z+1)^2=36."></span></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 3.29 · p. 79</div>

::: {.notes}
OneNote: x=5+2λ, y=1−λ, z=−3−2λ. Substitute to get (2+2λ)²+(−1−λ)²+(−2−2λ)²=36, hence 9(λ+1)²=36. Therefore λ=1 or −3. The corresponding points are (7,0,−5) and (−1,4,3). Both give squared distance 36 from centre (3,2,−1). Suggested, not official, 3-mark allocation: 1 for substituting all three components into the sphere; 1 for both parameter values; 1 for both points. This particular line passes through the centre at λ=−1, so the intersection points are the endpoints of a diameter; this is an optional bridge to the next slide, not a fact true of every secant.
:::
